classification.difficultyReason: Apply the two stated validity conditions to six given probability tables.

content.prompt: Identify which of the following represents a valid probability distribution. Remember that all probabilities must be between 0 and 1, and sum to 1.

answer.worked: All probabilities are between 0 and 1, and $0.1+0.6+0.2+0.1=1$. The distribution is valid.
$0.5+0.3-0.2+0.4=1$, but $P(X=3)=-0.2<0$. A probability cannot be negative, so the distribution is not valid.
All probabilities are between 0 and 1, and $0.25+0.25+0.25+0.25=1$. The distribution is valid.
Each probability is between $0\%$ and $100\%$, and $30\%+20\%+40\%+10\%=100\%=1$. The distribution is valid.
$0.7+0.2+0.4+0.2=1.5\ne1$. The probabilities do not sum to 1, so the distribution is not valid.

All probabilities are between 0 and 1.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac16+\frac13+\frac14+\frac14&=\frac2{12}+\frac4{12}+\frac3{12}+\frac3{12}\\&=1\end{aligned}$$
The distribution is valid.
